title: Long-term moderate PM2.5 exposure increases circulatory disease among US soldiers
source_unit: US Army soldiers, annual PM2.5 exposure, duty-station assignment, circulatory disease, hypertension, respiratory disease, and duration of exposure

observations.period: Working paper issued October 2026; roughly 150,000 US Army soldiers followed across career duty stations

denominator.unit: approximately US Army soldiers in detailed personnel records

exposure_design.unit: high-resolution annual PM2.5 measures linked to personnel records; Army relocations provide quasi-random variation in initial duty-station assignments

circulatory_disease.unit: sustained PM2.5 exposure substantially increases circulatory disease

hypertension.unit: hypertension is particularly affected by sustained PM2.5 exposure

respiratory_conditions.unit: evidence on respiratory conditions is mixed and specification-sensitive

short_duration.unit: shorter exposure durations have little detectable effect

care_access.unit: uniform access to care helps separate physiological exposure effects from differential health-care access

observations.method: The paper links detailed Army personnel records to annual PM2.5 measures and instruments career-average exposure using quasi-random variation in initial duty-station assignments caused by Army relocation needs.
observations.uncertainty: The NBER abstract does not disclose effect sizes, confidence intervals, exact exposure thresholds, follow-up years, or all exclusion assumptions. Soldiers are healthier and more institutionally selected than the general population; the study does not measure household exposure, worker choice, local inequality, costs, or current civilian generalizability directly.
observations.subgroup: Young, initially healthy US Army soldiers, with disease-specific results for circulatory, hypertensive, and respiratory conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Duty-station assignment, occupational tasks, housing, behavior, deployment, and cumulative exposure may differ from the instrument’s assumptions; uniform care access improves internal comparison but does not erase selection or establish that every civilian population faces the same response.

related_sources.claim: Nursing-home inspections produce temporary responses while higher ratings predict relative mortality.
Medicaid nursing-home financing can expand volume toward lower-quality facilities and reduce one-year survival in the studied setting.
California nursing homes manipulate size around a staffing threshold, limiting access particularly for disadvantaged patients.

boundary: This record adds a long-duration environmental-health layer to the US industrial/consumer program. It does not disclose effect sizes, establish universal civilian effects, measure household pollution, costs, worker choice, local political response, or a complete climate-health pathway in the same unit.
